CAST-1.title: Replay stamped a new receive time

CAST-2.title: An error answer that still committed

CAST-3.title: Retry after a lost answer re-inserted rows

CAST-4.title: GC deleted a slot a writer later retried into

CAST-8.title: RefCell borrow held across an await

CAST-9.title: One 1 MiB value made an object 40× larger

CAST-11.title: Configs carried static keys that shadowed IRSA and Pod Identity

CAST-12.title: Tests ran against binaries built from a different tree

CAST-13.title: A worker took a lease that was still live

CAST-14.title: A backlog longer than the lease window livelocked a worker

CAST-15.title: A 412 on the worker's own lease or checkpoint write dropped the lane

CAST-16.title: The count check could silently return short counts

CAST-17.title: A span's Duration was dropped when its start or end time was 0

CAST-18.title: A log body of integer 0 or double 0 read back as empty; an attribute's −0.0 read back as 0

CAST-19.title: Half-precision floats inside arrays and maps read back as null

CAST-20.title: A lost lease-renewal or checkpoint write dropped a lane that was still ours

CAST-21.title: The lane watermark could pass a request still in flight in a later-named epoch

CAST-22.title: A test script deleted the shared `otel` bucket, with every agent's test data in it

CAST-23.title: An unanswered announcement insert was not waited out, so it could land after the lane's lease changed hands

CAST-24.title: The entity aggregator pasted S3 object key, cluster and lane names into the text of its `ingest_log` and `lane_progress` INSERTs; a key with a quote under cluster `c1` forged a `c2` `ingest_log` row (`put_at` 2100), `c2` was never ingested, and every pass stopped at that object

CAST-25.title: The plan service's documented minimum URL lifetime (`url_ttl_s` 60) with the default `replan_margin_s` (60) gave `replan_after` equal to the signing time; a larger margin put it before signing. Every plan was stale when issued, so a client obeying X8 re-planned until its limit and never read

CAST-26.title: The query service labels an event-time window `complete` as soon as `complete_through` (a bound on `received_at`, custody time) reaches the window's end (`completeness/watermark.go` `MakeLabel`: `w.ToNs > ct`). A row whose event time is in the window but that is received later is missing from a result labelled complete

CAST-27.title: Near miss: agents sharing one checkout's git index. The alerts agent's staged edits landed in the lake UI agent's commit 9835f2f, and its own first commit, built from a private index on a stale base, would have reverted the coordinator's CAST commit 5f13738

CAST-28.title: Fork patch 0001 (overflow modes pinned to throw) left a jest expectation in `clickhouse.test.ts` without the pins, so the suite failed; the patch had never had its tests run

CAST-29.title: `@clickhouse/client` 1.23 replaces a per-query `Authorization` header with its own Basic header, so HyperDX's server-side queries (alerts, API, MCP) would reach the adapter with no token

CAST-30.title: All four role policies in `deploy/iam` (`edge-publisher`, `entity-controller`, `consumer`, `gc`) granted `s3:ListBucket` only under an `s3:prefix` condition. A HEAD/GET carries no `s3:prefix`, so on AWS a missing key answers 403, not 404: the consumer cannot read a missing `format.json` and exits; edge slots stay unresolved after any ambiguous PUT (403 is correctly kept unknown)

CAST-31.title: A ClickHouse SYNTAX_ERROR answer echoes the raw statement text, including the `s3()` access key, secret (and now session token); the consumer kept such errors in its logs and state unredacted

CAST-32.title: The query service's `metadata` scope (D25) served `SELECT * FROM system.tables` whole: `data_paths`, `metadata_path` (real server paths), `uuid`, `storage_policy`, sizes, and `system.databases.engine_full`, to any caller with the `query` role

CAST-33.title: Mosaic 0.31 names its pre-aggregated cube tables by a hash of their SQL and creates them `IF NOT EXISTS`; reloading different rows under the same table names (a new plan, a new window) leaves the old cubes answering. A chart showed 9,000 where 3,000 was right

CAST-34.title: The coordinator's spec (research/bitemporal.md §3) said a basis admits `received_at ≤ C`. The consumer promises only `received_at < complete_through`, and a pending object can carry `received_at` equal to it, so "same basis ⇒ same answer" would fail

CAST-35.title: The evaluator's late checks plus two replicas per identity exceeded the query service's default per-caller concurrency (4); the 429s counted as failed evaluations and paged "cannot evaluate"

CAST-36.title: Near miss: raising evaluator concurrency, the coordinator first added an `alert-evaluator` entry to queryd's `group_grants` (fleet scope) as well as to `limits`, and told team evaluators to join the group; a team identity would have gained fleet scope

CAST-37.title: A restarted entity controller dated every pod it had not yet seen from the pod's creation (`vf := created`); the aggregator merges `valid_from` as a minimum, so each restart moved a relabelled pod's current version back over its earlier versions: two versions valid at once in `pods` and `resources`, and the relabel time lost

CAST-38.title: Shared-resource exhaustion by agents, twice: a worktree Rust debug build (D29) and one-INSERT-per-object replay parts (D32, ~1.7 GB of part overhead) took free disk below 200 MB while other agents ran; builds and tests elsewhere failed or were cut short (D30's fork checks ran reduced)

CAST-39.title: The edge lane's append (Go `commit.Lane.Append`, Rust `runner::append`) resent without limit when every PUT got no answer and each HEAD found the slot free; the Go edge spun for 11 minutes at 40% CPU holding the lane mutex, blocking its heartbeats

CAST-40.title: parquet-go keeps a writer's footer key/value metadata across `Reset`, so the first unsplit object after a split one carried `oscope-part` in its footer; the Go edge also committed the two parts in a different order from Rust

CAST-41.title: **Recurrence of row 28.** Fork patch 0003's own jest expectation (`completeness.test.ts`, "reads the adapter headers") omitted the `atBasis: false` field 0003 added, so the suite failed; 0003 had been checked by transpiling and stubbing, never by running jest

CAST-42.title: A resource announcement statement arriving just past its fence, on a ClickHouse whose clock ran ahead, was skipped by the server's silent fence and answered with an empty OK; `announce_first` took that as landed, so the lane's rows were inserted before their announcements (`sameLane` broken; in another seed the announcements were never ingested)

CAST-43.title: Two tests had been skipping silently for lack of a bucket and were broken underneath: the horizon audit's end-to-end test wrote a format-v1 lane the consumer never discovers, and the announcements test compared quote-escaped TSV

CAST-44.title: Found by the retirement model, applies today without retirement: deleting a dead publisher pod's volume while a PUT it sent can still land lets that object arrive after the watermark has passed its custody time

CAST-45.title: D33 added `cluster` to the key/value rollups; conformance's `compare.py` listed the rollup columns by hand, so every conformance run since D33 died in the comparison

CAST-46.title: Two readers of parquetgo's schema broke silently when D21 (4d382ac) put `resource_id` and `resource_announce` ahead of the envelope: otap's `Flatten` wrote the envelope at a hard-coded field index and panicked on every batch (its `TestSmokeLocal` failed without any service), and `parquetgo/compare`'s `TestSameRowsAsChdb` kept a stale column expectation

CAST-47.title: Model and design gap: an earlier incarnation's zombie PUT could land after a later incarnation's close retired the lane; it fell below R and was quarantined although its request had been ingested (a false page), because a close was taken to seal the whole lane

CAST-48.title: Design gap: GC deletes slots ~2 minutes after the checkpoint passes them, so the only copy of a quarantined object would be gone before an operator could admit it

CAST-49.title: Near miss in the design: resolving score facts "latest by custody time" lets a retried older correction, received later, override a newer one

CAST-50.title: A consumer checkpoint PUT got no answer; the read-back showed the checkpoint unchanged, so the worker kept its old version (17), but the store applied the write later (next = 21). GC acts on the stored checkpoint and deleted slots 17–19; the worker's scan then waited at a "gap" at 17 forever: the lane stalled for good and nothing after it was ingested

CAST-51.title: Per-push CI was red for about 29 hours (runs 38–95, 09-27 23:05Z to 09-29 04:16Z: 28 failed, ~30 cancelled, none green), and the nightly was red from its first runs, including a Kani harness that stopped compiling on 09-28 because it is only built nightly. Nobody read the results

CAST-52.title: The query service's grants are a cluster set × a namespace set, not pairs: a principal granted `devtools/dev-payments` and `prod-eu-1/search` can also read `prod-eu-1/dev-payments` and `devtools/search` (`query/internal/auth/principal.go`)

CAST-53.title: Regression in the row 52 fix: the single-grant fallback in `sqlscope` read a literal `"*"` inside a cluster or namespace list as "all", and trimmed padded names (`"a "` → `"a"`); both had been refused as `bad_scope_value`. Also, `f846d66` was pushed after a local run that showed the failure, because a pipe hid the test's exit code

CAST-54.title: From D30 on, the lake UI and the Mosaic spike planned at the basis `latest` and **left out** everything received after `complete_through` — the lake-only rows D24 exists to show — with only a "N newer object(s) left out" note. Both nightly e2e suites failed at their first test, so 9 lake UI and 6 Mosaic tests after it never ran; three of those were broken too (expiry tests relying on a cached plan, no-watermark tests getting 503 on `latest`, Mosaic URL mode planning without a basis)

CAST-55.title: Agents dispatching the nightly with different `jobs` selections cancelled each other's queued runs: the dispatched lake UI e2e run (8) was replaced by another agent's dispatch (9) before it started, so the plan tail's first real e2e never ran

CAST-56.title: The nightly hegel fleet test reported a lost batch that was not lost: the harness judged the run finished once every row had landed, while one copy's announcement was still waiting for a legitimate lease takeover, and the final check then counted that announcement as missing

CAST-57.title: The lake UI test rig (lakeuirig) left the `otelcol-s3pq` edge processes it had started running after it exited, when it was signalled during setup

CAST-58.title: A consumer test that checks a refused-credentials error is redacted asserted that the text contained no "403"; the text names the object, whose random id sometimes contained 403, so the test failed about once in 700 runs

CAST-59.title: The Go-vs-Rust conformance comparison passed while comparing less data: both edges refused the two largest corpus requests (85 MB and 78 MB) as over the then 64 MiB request cap, identically, so nothing differed; `run.sh` logged the refusals and did not fail

CAST-60.title: Clippy in one agent's worktree used an `otap_s3pq` rmeta built from another agent's worktree through the shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR (same metadata hash, fingerprint looked fresh) and reported symbols missing that the code had

CAST-61.title: The nightly chdb comparison (CAST-46's only regression test) went red after two unrelated changes, neither of which dispatched it: the Go 1.27 upgrade changed how map and slice attributes render (121 differing trace rows), and the D36 offloader added `payload_refs`/`payloads` columns the chdb prototype does not write

CAST-62.title: The regression test for CAST-56 used a fixed 378 ms sleep to reach its failure shape; when D36 added a payload statement to each round, the sleep no longer reached the shape and the test would have passed without testing anything

CAST-63.title: ci.yml went red at 25fcbe3 because a sed edited a CAST record after its tables were rendered; the commit that fixed it (6ef251f) changed only Markdown, so paths-ignore skipped CI and no run verified the head. The STPA migration had made Markdown files CI inputs (records, generated sections, VERIFICATION.md cells) while the CAST-51 rule still treated every .md push as prose

CAST-64.title: The Go edge's lane serialised Append on a sync.Mutex held across its S3 requests, up to MaxResends resends with their timeouts: a caller queued behind a lane stuck in resends waited with no regard for its own deadline

CAST-65.title: A basis token was accepted in four spellings: base64url decoding ignored non-zero trailing bits, so one basis had several strings that all passed the MAC

CAST-66.title: The entity controller's work-queue goroutine leaked when Run failed (kube-system unreadable, a cache that never synced): Run shut the queue down on its normal exits only

CAST-67.title: `ingress.Bearer` returned ok with an empty token for "Bearer " followed by blanks

CAST-68.title: CI runs 133 and 135 died with "No space left on device" on the runner: Go caches for two toolchain versions plus the Rust build and the runner's preinstalled SDKs filled its disk; nightly build and rust-integration died the same way (runs 21, 22, 24)

CAST-69.title: Two destructive cleanups on the shared dev box: `rm -rf /tmp/go-build*` while other agents were building (it may have removed their in-flight build directories), and a `go clean -modcache` started by accident and killed within a second

H-1.title: Acknowledged telemetry is in no store and cannot be recovered

H-2.title: A result is presented as complete while it is missing or duplicating data

H-3.title: Telemetry is attributed to the wrong entity, or to none

H-4.title: An alert condition holds but no page reaches on-call, or a page fires for a condition that does not hold

H-5.title: People act on a stale or wrong view without knowing it (snapshot, source or mode confusion)

H-6.title: An unauthorized party can read or write telemetry, the catalog or control objects

H-7.title: A pipeline component uses resources beyond its budget

H-8.title: The pipeline cannot accept, ingest or serve telemetry while an incident needs it: a lane stalls, writes are refused, or queries fail closed

H-E1.title: Telemetry is committed under a tenant its sender is not entitled to write, or attributed to a person who did not send it

H-E2.title: A party that is not an authenticated member of the organisation, on the organisation's terms (device compliance, the right client), can write telemetry

H-E3.title: Device telemetry is readable beyond its owner's scope: in the device buffer (stolen or shared laptop), in transit, or at query time through a grant that over-reaches

H-E4.title: Telemetry the forwarder acknowledged to a tool is dropped without the drop being counted and visible

H-E5.title: One principal's volume or request rate exhausts the ingress, its lanes, central or the budget

H-E6.title: A retry or a replay is counted twice

H-E7.title: The ingress uses its own authority (its S3 credential, its lanes) for something the caller could not do itself (confused deputy)

H-E8.title: People read ingress attribution as more than it proves (authorship of content, or a device), or trust a view with devtools data missing without knowing

H-E9.title: Sign-in friction makes the tool unusable (prompts, blocking calls on the tool's path)

H-G1.title: **Over-grant**: a principal can read or write beyond what any one grant intended (a product of grants, a role borrowed from another grant, an environment crossed)

H-G2.title: **Under-grant during response**: a responder cannot read the cluster, environment or plan they need, or learns it only mid-incident

H-G3.title: **Drift**: the query service's check and the storage layer's (IAM) disagree, so one path grants what the other refuses, or a policy change reaches one and not the other

H-G4.title: **Escalation through authoring**: a grant author (or a compromised author account) widens their own or another's scope, or writes a policy whose meaning differs from its reading

H-G5.title: **Confused deputy**: the query service, holding read on every cluster, presigns or reads for a caller something the caller may not read

H-G6.title: **Break-glass**: emergency access is unavailable when needed, or outlives the emergency, or is used without a record

H-G7.title: **Environment crossover**: a dev (or stg) principal, workload or credential reads or writes prd, or prd data lands in a dev store

H-G8.title: **Person data disclosed**: an object id resolved to a name, or a person's team history, for a reader not entitled to it; or kept after erasure

H-L1.title: Prompt or completion content is readable outside its tenant's scope, by a role that needs only metadata, or by an existence probe (a content hash)

H-L2.title: A cost figure is presented as correct while computed from a price table that was stale, wrong or changed since, or while tokens were double counted

H-L3.title: An evaluated result (a score aggregate, an experiment comparison, a dashboard) changes after it was acted on, and nothing shows that it changed or that more scores could still arrive

H-L4.title: An LLM trace or session is shown as complete while spans, content or scores are still missing (long agent runs, streaming, edge outages)

H-L5.title: Payload volume exhausts an edge buffer, an object, a lane or central (MB prompts, hostile values)

H-L6.title: Content from a less-trusted writer is interpreted as code or instructions: attribute names or references spliced into SQL, markup rendered, **prompt injection** into an LLM-as-judge or a UI assistant that reads traces

H-L7.title: An erasure or retention obligation is not met, or is met by rewriting history under an answer that promised not to change

H-L8.title: Two versions of one observation or score are both counted, or a partial update overwrites a field with an older or empty value

L-1.title: An incident is missed, misdiagnosed or prolonged because operators lacked correct telemetry

L-3.title: Telemetry shown to people or alerts is wrong: duplicated, missing, stale or on the wrong entity

L-4.title: Sensitive data is disclosed (secrets or personal data in logs, one team's data to another)

L-5.title: Telemetry or the catalog is tampered with, hiding or forging activity

L-6.title: The pipeline harms production or budget: node pressure, full disks, runaway central or S3 cost

L-7.title: A model, prompt or release decision is made on wrong evaluation or cost figures

L-E1.title: The telemetry harms the developer's own work: the tool blocks, slows, or prompts for sign-in repeatedly, and people disable it (which in turn is L-1 for the teams relying on it)

L-G1.title: The organisation cannot say who could read what, when (an auditor's or a data subject's question goes unanswered or is answered wrongly)

LS-1.title: The edge crashed after a commit landed but before the buffer's ack; on replay it stamped a new receive time, so the copy fell outside the check horizon

LS-2.title: ClickHouse answered a timeout, but the insert committed up to 29 s later; the consumer's process model said "failed"

LS-3.title: A writer that never learned its write succeeded retried into a slot GC had already deleted, below the checkpoint

LS-4.title: A worker paused past its lease; its clock said it still held the lane

LS-5.title: The entity controller was down or lagging; agents kept producing telemetry for pods the catalog lacked

LS-6.title: Central was degraded; the query service fell back to the lake but the UI kept its "live" look

LS-7.title: A lane was lagging; the alert window closed on partial data and read as "no errors"

LS-8.title: The alerting engine could not reach any source and treated "no data" as "OK"

LS-9.title: The buffer volume filled before the size cap; the publisher crash-looped

LS-10.title: Retention was cut while an edge site was offline for days; its replay landed in expired partitions

R-E1.title: The tenant and the person are asserted by the ingress from a verified Entra token and operator policy only; every producer claim is removed from the tenant keys and kept, if at all, as a label

R-E2.title: Tokens: v2.0, RS256, allowed tenant GUIDs, `iss` = `{authority}/{tid}/v2.0`, tenant-bound keys honoured, audience = the ingress API, `azp` in an allow-list, delegated scope for users, app role for workloads

R-E3.title: Identity and admission before the body; compressed, decoded and item caps; per-principal budgets

R-E4.title: Stamping is a pure function of (request bytes, attribution): no time, token id or replica in the bytes

R-E5.title: 200 only after the edge's commit verdict; 503 with `Retry-After` when unresolved; the D35 close only with no handler running

R-E6.title: The forwarder resends each request's bytes unchanged, only under the token of the person who produced it, and never prompts on the tool's path

R-E7.title: The forwarder keeps no disk buffer: a small bounded in-memory queue only, nothing persisted on the device; every drop (queue full, a long outage, a crash, no token) is counted on the device and never blocks the tool (owner revision, D37)

R-E8.title: Query grants are explicit `(cluster, namespace)` pairs; a devtools namespace never equals a Kubernetes namespace until then

R-E9.title: Conditional Access for the ingress API requires a compliant device and allows only the forwarder and workload clients

R-G1.title: A principal's scope for a role is the union of the `(role, cluster, namespace)` tuples of its grants; never a product across grants or roles. Rows, dictionary guards, catalog ids and plans are cut by it

R-G2.title: A plan (presigned raw objects) is given only for clusters granted whole for `plan`

R-G3.title: Grants are authored in one language (Cedar) and compiled; a policy outside the enforceable fragment is refused at authoring time with a reason, never compiled in part

R-G4.title: The compiled output equals Cedar's authorizer on every request of the registry's universe, checked in CI

R-G5.title: Policy changes by code review (two approvals, CODEOWNERS), with the compiled effect in the diff; principals are groups, never persons by name

R-G6.title: Environments are separated at the storage layer (a bucket, better an account, per environment); a cluster belongs to one environment, by a registry that also gates its writes

R-G7.title: The query service's presign credentials read one cluster per session (defence in depth)

R-G8.title: Break-glass is time-bound group membership (PIM), approved and recorded; grants themselves never expire silently or stay silently

R-G9.title: A person's name resolves only for readers holding `resolve_person` on the row's namespace; erasure is a fact applied at every basis

R-L1.title: The tenant of every LLM span, payload and score is the (cluster, namespace) the edge derived from its own resource detection; SDK-claimed projects and keys are labels at most

R-L2.title: Content (prompts, completions, tool arguments and results, system instructions) is readable only through the query service, under the same scope as its rows **and** an `llm_content` right; every content read is audited with the references read; content hashes are keyed per tenant

R-L3.title: Cost is computed at query time from price facts with valid time and system time; every cost result names the price facts' as-of and counts spans with no price; SDK-provided costs are shown as such, never mixed silently

R-L4.title: The edge offloads any value above a threshold by reference, caps value, request and nesting size, marks every truncation and redaction with the original size, and counts each; caps and thresholds are validated together at start (CAST 25)

R-L5.title: Evaluated results carry their basis and a settle status (scores received through; the policy's settle window); evaluators read through the query service at a basis and score only settled traces

R-L6.title: Scores, corrections, deletions and annotations are append-only facts with a custody time, a stable id, the fact they supersede, a source and an author set by the writer's identity; resolution at the basis is the unsuperseded fact (latest by custody, flagged, if two); retractions hide, never erase

R-L7.title: No name, key, reference or content from a producer is spliced into SQL or a path; references are validated (32 hex) and resolved in the query tree

R-L8.title: Content is never passed to a model or a renderer as instructions or markup: delimited as data for evaluators and assistants, rendered as text or sanitised markdown in the UI

R-L9.title: A row is committed only with, or after, the payloads it references (same object, payload part first); a dangling reference is counted and shown, never silently empty

R-L10.title: Erasure is a fact (a tombstone that hides at query time, effective at once) plus, where the owner requires, a physical purge that is recorded as an epoch; a basis older than a purge says so instead of answering differently

R-L11.title: No storage engine merge decides which version of a fact wins (no `ReplacingMergeTree`/`FINAL` or `min`/`anyLast` aggregation for correctness); duplicates of an identical fact are harmless by construction

R-L12.title: The GenAI semantic-convention mapping is policy (a versioned table), each row records the convention and producer scope it was mapped from, and a mapping change runs every consumer of the mapped columns

R-S1.title: Every result carries its source and complete-through time for its own scope (the clusters and signals it reads, named in the result; D29), and which event time that settles (D26); the UI shows them on every view

R-S2.title: Windows not yet complete are drawn as incomplete, and counts over them are marked partial

R-S3.title: Alerts evaluate only up to the complete-through time of the rule's own scope (D29), plus the lateness bound (D26); a failed or unevaluable window pages

R-S4.title: Silences and pinned snapshots have an owner and an expiry, shown at handoff

R-S5.title: Views show catalog lag and rows without an entity match

R-S6.title: Retention changes are refused if shorter than the longest configured edge-buffer outage (custody age; see DECISIONS.md D19)

R-S7.title: Writes are scoped by cluster prefix and role; edge keys cannot delete; the aggregator rejects mismatched clusters. Scheme (built with format v2, 2026-09-27): cluster-first keys; publishers and entity controllers may only create under their own cluster's prefix, keyed on a cluster principal tag in the session credentials; only consumer roles can write or delete control objects. Recorded in [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md) D18

R-S8.title: Reads are role-scoped by cluster and namespace; every query is audit-logged

R-S9.title: The query service and rewrite proxy build SQL only from a parsed tree, with per-user limits

R-S10.title: Alerts group by entity and cause, one page per incident

SC-1.title: Telemetry must not be acknowledged until it is durable, and must be ingested exactly once

SC-2.title: Every result must state its source and the time it is complete through; incomplete windows must be marked

SC-3.title: Entity attribution must be derived from the resource's own attributes and must fall back to them when the catalog is missing or late

SC-4.title: Alerts must evaluate only complete windows and must report their own failure to evaluate

SC-5.title: The UI must make its data source, snapshot and degraded mode visible on every view

SC-6.title: Every write path must be authenticated and authorized, and reads must be scoped by role

SC-7.title: Every component must have a resource budget and must push back rather than exceed it

SC-8.title: Every component must keep accepting, ingesting and serving telemetry, or say visibly that it cannot; every retry on an unknown outcome must be bounded and hand back to a caller that can back off

SEC-1.title: A compromised pod or node forges telemetry or entity records for other workloads

SEC-2.title: A stolen edge key overwrites or deletes lane objects

SEC-3.title: An attacker writes a lease or checkpoint to stall or skip lanes

SEC-4.title: Secrets or personal data in log bodies and attributes

SEC-5.title: A crafted query exhausts central or the lake readers

SEC-6.title: An insider silences alerts or edits rules to hide activity

SEC-7.title: Log injection makes the UI or proxy run unintended SQL

SEC-8.title: Tampered time on an edge node shifts receive times

UCA-10.title: Central was degraded; the query service fell back to the lake but the UI kept its "live" look

UCA-12.title: The alerting engine could not reach any source and treated "no data" as "OK"

qs-\u003elake/control/reads.title: Route a query to a source
